subject: Operational readiness & staffing matrix for VPC/on-prem pilot
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Park <alan@brightline.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational readiness & staffing matrix for VPC/on-prem pilot

Team — attaching a first-pass staffing & responsibilities matrix for the Brightline VPC/on‑prem pilot (vpc-resource-matrix.xlsx) and a rough network diagram. Brightline has asked for a firm launch window in Q4; before we commit I want to align cross-functionally on the minimal team we need for a safe pilot and what exceptions (SLA, data residency, onprem access) require leadership approval.

Key asks: 
- Can infra commit 2 FTEs for the pilot-week ops oncall (pre/post launch)? (Kimberly)
- What architecture reviewers do we need to sign off for an on-prem tenancy? (Karthik)
- CS/AM scope for customer coordination & runbook ownership? (Neha)
- Can runtime commit to a conservative kernel/quantization matrix for the first pilot? (Marcus)

I've marked cells in the matrix that I think are negotiable vs. hard-requirements. Please review the matrix and ping me with any gating items by EOD Tue so I can consolidate and respond to Alan with a timeline.

Attachments: vpc-resource-matrix.xlsx, network-diagram.pdf

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational readiness & staffing matrix for VPC/on-prem pilot

Thanks for the deck — I skimmed the matrix. Quick notes: 
- Two dedicated infra FTEs for pilot-week ops is optimistic. Our current priority runs through mid‑Nov for dedicated changes. We can do 1.0 FTE (senior infra eng) + 0.5 SRE support on-call, but that assumes reduced rollback SLAs and no on‑site access requirements.
- If Brightline requires network peering changes on their DC side (and DatacenterOps needs to be engaged), there will be a 2–3 week lead time for change windows and approvals.

Action items for me: I'll confirm whether we can shift the second FTE from a capacity buffer. If leadership approves a temporary exception for pilot posture we can staff to 2 FTEs.

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational readiness & staffing matrix for VPC/on-prem pilot

Jasmine — thanks for pulling this together. From runtime/serving perspective: 
- For the pilot we should aim for a single quantization profile (int8) and a vetted kernel set to minimize unknown perf regressions. That will let us commit to a predictable memory/profile and reduce on-call burden.
- We will need 1 runtime engineer full-time for the 2 weeks around launch plus 0.25 FTE for the first month of monitoring & mitigations.
- If Brightline expects 99.9% latency SLA on the private endpoint, we should flag that as an enterprise exception; it materially changes our routing/fallback story.

I'll put conservative estimates into the matrix and flag the cells that require SLA exceptions. Also: Karthik, I need your input on whether the proposed network diagram supports our caching strategy (sticky routing + KV cache locality).

Best,
Marcus
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational readiness & staffing matrix for VPC/on-prem pilot

Team — quick technical read: 
- The network-diagram.pdf is a helpful start but misses two critical controls: (1) a customer-isolated NAT/egress filter layer for data exfil protection, and (2) an audited jump host pattern for any vendor/Redwood engineers accessing on‑prem hosts. Both are non-negotiable for me unless Security signs an exception.
- The pilot topology as drawn will fragment KV cache locality across AZs; that increases tail latency risk. If we accept that for pilot we must bake in a higher token-cost buffer for retries and add observability hooks for per-request cache hits.

Estimated infra delta: additional 40–60 engineering-hours to stand up the NAT/egress controls and 20 hours to implement the audited jump host + onboarding docs.

CC: DatacenterOps to confirm lead times for building the NAT/peering rules.

-Karthik
Staff Engineer, Platform Architecture
Redwood Inference
From: Alan Park <alan@brightline.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational readiness & staffing matrix for VPC/on-prem pilot

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. A few data points from Brightline side: 
- We are aiming for a soft launch window the week of Oct 18 (internal product priorities could move this a week earlier or later).
- We can accept an initial higher-latency pilot if it means you can reduce on-site staffing; our priority is data locality and an isolated tenancy for HIPAA-scoped workloads.
- Brightline legal will want the list of controls for egress/ingress and the jump-host audit before we sign off. Can you share a short runbook and the NAT/egress control spec?

If it's helpful, I can loop in DatacenterOps' network lead to coordinate change windows — they are flexible but would prefer a 2–3 week lead time notice.

Appreciate the clear asks. Please let me know what you want Brightline to approve/commit to vs. what you need Redwood leadership to sign off on.

—Alan
VP, Infrastructure & Security
Brightline
